annotations.title: Which sequencing reads actually tell your candidates apart

description: Given the molecules a cloning reaction could have produced and the sequencing primers you could use, work out which primers separate which pairs of candidates — and return the smallest set that separates every pair any of them can. Scores a read by discrimination, not coverage: a read of 700 bases every candidate shares is worth nothing, and a short read across a junction is worth everything. Names the pairs no primer here separates, so you find out before paying for the reads rather than after. Pair it with outcome_deconvolve once the traces come back.

candidates.description: The molecules this reaction could produce, as { id, label, sequence, circular? }. Between 2 and 24; assembly_outcomes' intended plus alternatives is the intended source.

maxMismatches.description: Mismatch budget passed to the priming scan. Defaults to primer-binding's own (~10% of the primer's length).

primers.description: Sequencing primers to choose between, as { id, label, sequence }. Up to 32.

usableFrom.description: Bases after the primer's 3' end before the trace becomes readable (0-500). A difference inside this dead zone is not counted as a separation, because the trace cannot show it.

usableLength.description: Readable bases per reaction, counted from usableFrom (50-5000).
